summary: Cameron Kyle Bender Foltz is a scholar in religious studies and Tibetology. He earned his MA at Florida State University (~2016–2018) under supervisor Bryan J. Cuevas, committee members Kristina Buhrman and Joseph Hellweg, and teacher Jimmy Yu.

Camillo Alessio Formigatti is an Indologist who studied at the University of Milan (~1999–2004). He taught Sanskrit at SOAS (~2010–2012) and held posts at the University of Cambridge (2011–2014) and Bodleian Libraries (~2013).

Carl Bielefeldt works in Buddhist studies and Japanology. He studied with Shunryu Suzuki (~1967–1971) and earned his Ph.D. at UC Berkeley (~1974–1980). His career includes serving on an editorial board at Stanford University (~1980–2015).

Carl Cappeller (1840–1925) was an Indology and linguistics scholar. He studied at Berlin (1860–1864) under Bopp and Weber, Königsberg (~1860–1868), Leipzig (PhD by 1868), and Jena (habilitation ~1870–1872), where he became Professor in 1872.

Carl Friedrich Gauss (1777–1855) studied at Collegium Carolinum (1792–1795), the University of Göttingen (1795–1798), and the University of Helmstedt (~1799). He later held a post at the University of Göttingen (~1807–1855).
Carl Gaedicke is a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He completed his PhD at the University of Jena (~1875–1877), studying under Berthold Delbrück, Eduard Sievers, and Carl Cappeller.

Carl Olson specializes in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Indology. Mentored by John Y. Fenton (~1973–1977), he served as Teacher-Scholar Chair in the Humanities at Allegheny College (~1981–2017) and was a fellow at Clare Hall, Cambridge.

Carl Shigeo Yamamoto is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Virginia (~2003–2009), supervised by Jeffrey Hopkins and David Germano, with Kurtis R. Schaeffer on his committee.

Carl Siegfried (1830–1903) worked in Indology and religious studies. He studied under Albrecht Weber and Rudolf von Roth at Halle-Wittenberg and Bonn. He held posts at Schulpforta (~1865–1875), Trinity College Dublin, and the University of Jena (~1875–1903).

Carl W. Ernst (born 1950) is a scholar of religious studies and Indology. He studied at Stanford University (~1968–1973) and Harvard University (~1973–1981), and served as a professor at UNC Chapel Hill from 1992 to 2022.
Carl Wilhelm Vollgraff (1876–1967) was a scholar in linguistics, history, and archaeology. He held posts at the University of Groningen (1908–1916) and Utrecht University (1917–1946).

Carlo Giussani (1840–1900) was an Indology and linguistics scholar. He studied at the Scuola Normale Superiore (~1859–1863) and under Giuseppe Bardelli (~1860–1863), Albrecht Weber (1863), and Rudolf von Roth (~1864–1865).

Carlo Jamelle Harris is a scholar in philosophy and Buddhist studies. He earned a Master of Arts in Philosophy at National Chengchi University (~2005–2009), where he was supervised by Chen-kuo Lin alongside committee member Yao-ming Tsai.

Carmen Blacker (1924–2009) specialized in Japanology and religious studies. She studied at Somerville College (~1953–1955) and under Shigeru Gorai (1977–1981), serving as Lecturer in Japanese at the University of Cambridge (~1955–1991).

Carmen Dragonetti (1937–2018) was an Indologist and philosopher educated at National University of San Marcos. She was a professor at the University of Buenos Aires, vice director of Instituto de Investigaciones Budistas (~1989–2018), and held fellowships at IIBS and Nyingma Institute.

Carmen Meinert is a Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Sinology scholar. She earned her PhD at the University of Bonn (~1997–2001) under Wolfgang Kubin and Jens-Uwe Hartmann, and held posts at the University of Hamburg (~2006–2010) and Ruhr University Bochum (~2013).

Carol S. Anderson is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. She completed her PhD at the University of Chicago (~1994), studying under W. S. Karunatillake and John A. Brinkman, and became Associate Professor of Religion at Kalamazoo College (~1993).

Carola Roloff (born 1959) works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. She earned her PhD at the University of Hamburg (~2003–2008) under David P. Jackson, and held posts at Tibetisches Zentrum Hamburg and Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies (2006–2007).

Carola S. Carstens specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She completed her doctorate at the University of Hamburg (by 2005) under Lambert Schmithausen and David P. Jackson, and held posts at Rice University (1998–1999) and Hamburg.

Carole McGranahan (born 1969) is a Tibetology and anthropology scholar who studied at Colgate and the University of Michigan (PhD 1999–2002). She was an Assistant Professor of Anthropology at the University of Colorado Boulder (~2001–2008).
